355956.title: Yip's maximal subfield clique conjecture for generalized Paley graphs
355956.literal_statement: Let $d>1$ be an integer. Let $q \equiv 1 \pmod {2d}$ be a power of a prime $p$, and let $r$ be the largest integer such that $d \mid \frac{q-1}{p^r-1}$. The subfield $\mathbb{F}_{p^r}$ is a clique in the generalized Paley graph $GP(q,d)=\operatorname{Cay}(\mathbb{F}_q^+;(\mathbb{F}_q^*)^d)$. **Yip's maximal subfield clique conjecture.** The subfield $\mathbb{F}_{p^r}$ forms a maximal clique in $GP(q,d)$. This conjecture asserts that the largest subfield producing a subfield clique cannot be extended to a larger clique. The paper resolves it in a stronger form under a sufficient-size hypothesis, while the unrestricted statement is the conjecture being addressed.

355701.title: Partial converse for monochromatic triangles in symmetric $v_{3}$ configurations
355701.literal_statement:
Let a **symmetric $v_{3}$ configuration** be a configuration whose lines are arranged so that each line contains three points and each point lies on three lines. Suppose such a configuration contains a maximal set of mutually intersecting lines of size $i$. A **line $2$-coloring** assigns one of two colors to each line, and a monochromatic triangle is a triangle whose three lines have the same color. **Partial converse conjecture.** If the minimum number of monochromatic triangles over all line $2$-colorings is non-zero, then

$$
i>4.
$$

This conjecture proposes a partial converse to the preceding theorem relating the size of mutually intersecting line sets to the minimum number of monochromatic triangles. The supplied text gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
